question.problem:
The weights of a particular breed of geese are normally distributed with a mean of $7\,\text{kg}$ and a standard deviation of $1\,\text{kg}.$ Suppose $4$ geese are randomly selected. What is the probability that the mean weight for this sample will be more than $6.8\,\text{kg},$ but less than $7\,\text{kg}?$ *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.4\,$ $\,0.3446\,$ $\,0.3409\,$ $\,0.3372\,$
$\,-0.3\,$ $\,0.3821\,$ $\,0.3783\,$ $\,0.3745\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.4207\,$ $\,0.4168\,$ $\,0.4129\,$

$z$ $\,0.00\,$ $\,0.01\,$ $\,0.02\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4602\,$ $\,0.4562\,$ $\,0.4522\,$
$\,0.0\,$ $\,0.5000\,$ $\,0.4960\,$ $\,0.4920\,$
$\,0.1\,$ $\,0.5398\,$ $\,0.5359\,$ $\,0.5319\,$
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

 then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

We're told that the population mean $\mu =7,$ the population standard deviation $\sigma =1,$ and that the sample size $n=4.$ Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(7,\frac{{1}^{2}}{4}) \\  & ∼N(7,0.25).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(6.8<\overset{―}{X}<7).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(6.8<\overset{―}{X}<7) & =P(\frac{6.8-7}{\sqrt{0.25}}<Z<\frac{7-7}{\sqrt{0.25}}) \\  & =P(-0.4<Z<0) \\  & =Φ(0)-Φ(-0.4) \\  & =0.5-Φ(-0.4)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
Φ(-0.4)=0.3446.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(6.8<\overset{―}{X}<7) & =0.5-Φ(-0.4) \\  & =0.5-0.3446 \\  & =0.1554.\end{aligned}
$$
